parsed.explanation: The operative regime is protective on paper and in practice: no trans-specific criminal statute, no visitor-facing facility or border restrictions, official rules for housing trans detainees (documented 2025, though unread in detail), hate-crime aggravation, and enforcement that acted — 15 arrests after the March 2025 dating-app ambush network. That network is the principal drag: organised queer-targeted violence, filmed and shared, current in 2025, though targeting is documented for gay/bisexual men, not trans visitors specifically. Hate-crime totals (1,575 violent-prejudice victims) lack denominators and trans breakdowns, so magnitude is unresolved, not proven elevated. The far-right electoral surge is climate risk, not operative law. Broad social acceptance and community infrastructure lower everyday exposure. Sits below 0.85 because of the documented organised-violence wave, above 0.65 because no visitor detention, exclusion or state hostility is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented; X/indeterminate/no-marker documents are recognised and LGR needs no surgery, so no border mismatch exposure is recorded.
entry_documents.protection: Constitutional Court ruling (2018) requiring accurate gender recognition; X passports issued since 2019.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor's home-issued documents face no documented additional scrutiny at entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented as adverse; official rules on housing transgender prisoners exist but their specific provisions were not read, leaving placement rules an open question.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2025 national research report documents gender self-determination and anti-discrimination protection in detention; justice ministry issued official housing rules (2025).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If a trans visitor is detained, the ministry's written housing rules are the citable authority.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Rejected petition for queer sauna time slots (2025) — a single administrative refusal, no broader facility restriction documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Goods-and-services anti-discrimination coverage in every federal state since January 2017; gender-inclusive forms guidance (2025).
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State-level protections apply uniformly; documented sequencing gap is historical, not a current rights difference.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitors; resident-facing psychiatric-opinion conditions on recognition and treatment are a resident rule only.
care_services.protection: Puberty-blocker care endorsed by national medical societies; documented health-system engagement with gender care.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor's care access faces no documented visitor-specific bar.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Neo-Nazi network using fake dating profiles to lure and ambush victims, filming them and accusing them of paedophilia — threat-framing by non-state actors; far-right party won most votes (2024), raising future-direction concern.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Police arrested 15 suspects; hate-crime aggravation in law; Security Police Act obliges unbiased policing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State treated the network as criminal, not as policy; state is currently responder, not perpetrator.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented; education-ministry rules restricting outside sex-ed providers touch programming, not visiting minors or guardians.
minors_guardians.protection: National medical societies endorse youth gender care; conversion-therapy association banned (2019).
minors_guardians.interaction: No documented visitor-specific rule affecting travel with a minor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Current (2025) documented wave of organised ambushes (17+ known victims, believed higher); 1,575 violent-prejudice victims in 2025 without per-capita or trans breakdown — magnitude unresolved, police acknowledge under-recording.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Law-enforcement arrests, hate-speech ban, aggravating-factor treatment; transphobic incidents reported declining.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Dating-app users, including trans visitors, are plausibly within the lure pattern even if not documented targets.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unknowns: exact trans-detainee housing provisions (unread German document); trans-specific hate-crime magnitude; whether trans people were among ambush victims.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning enforcement demonstrated by arrests; open advocacy infrastructure.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions are lighter than documented exposures under the rubric; none resolves toward danger on the structural record.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar structure: equality protections, public violence in identifiable settings, police who act when evidence is clear. This dossier adds a documented organised violence network but also documented arrests of its members; protections here are broader and more recently documented, so it sits slightly above 0.75-D.

0.85-A has isolated friction and functioning oversight; here an organised, filmed ambush campaign is documented as current, plus under-recorded hate-crime volume. That documented pattern keeps the rating below 0.85-A despite comparably strong legal machinery.

0.65-D shows an actual visitor detained and searched before remedy. No visitor detention, ejection or state hostility is documented here; enforcement prosecuted the perpetrator network. This case sits clearly above 0.65-D.

0.45-D turns routine registration into universal exposure through mandatory marker disclosure. Here no universal-exposure mechanism is documented at all — documents may carry X or no marker — so the gap below this jurisdiction is large.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is one where law and institutions work largely FOR trans visitors: no criminal statute touches expression, documents can be made to match, detention rules for transgender people officially exist, and the state demonstrably prosecutes those who commit anti-LGBT violence — 15 arrests after a filmed ambush network. The principal documented exposure is that same network plus a general hate-crime volume whose trans-specific share and per-capita magnitude the sources do not resolve; a trans visitor using dating apps plausibly shares the ambush exposure even though documented victims were gay/bisexual men. State is responder, not threat-framer, though the far-right electoral surge marks the trajectory as uncertain. Resident-facing gaps (psychiatric-opinion conditions on recognition, missing expungement scheme) do not reach the visitor. Open questions on detention placement and violence magnitude hold the score below 0.80 but do not convert to exposure on this record.
